set.body: These modules call cliWrappers.ts's callLLM directly, which uses Bun.spawn -- only callable from a real Bun process, never from browser-executed React code (Bun is undefined in the browser; confirmed via typeof Bun === 'undefined' in a live browser test). DiagramGenExtension.tsx hit this exact bug during epic C story 1 and was fixed by routing through src/lib/llmClient.ts (Tauri run_llm_cli command, or the dev server's POST /api/llm) instead of calling cliWrappers.callLLM directly. Epic B's per-note enrichment action (wiring ContentInjector into the toolbar) will hit the same failure the moment it's actually clicked in the UI unless it goes through llmClient.ts too.

set.body: DOMPurify's svg-only sanitize profile in src/lib/sanitize.ts hard-excludes the foreignObject tag (a known SVG XSS vector), which is how Mermaid renders flowchart/state-diagram node labels (HTML span/p inside foreignObject, not plain SVG <text>). Result: node shapes render but all label text is silently stripped. Fixed by adding the html DOMPurify profile, ADD_TAGS:['foreignobject'], and HTML_INTEGRATION_POINTS:{foreignobject:true} (DOMPurify enforces HTML-in-SVG namespace rules independently of the tag allowlist). Verified live: flowchart labels (Start/Is it working?/Yes/No/Great!/Debug) now render correctly.
set.title: sanitizeSvg strips Mermaid's HTML-based node labels (foreignObject), leaving diagrams with empty shapes and no text

set.body: Observed while live-verifying the sanitizeSvg fix: when an AI-generated diagram has invalid Mermaid syntax, DiagramGenExtension.tsx correctly catches the error and shows its own inline message, but mermaid.render() itself also has a side effect of appending a bomb-icon error overlay to document.body -- outside any of our React-managed containers, appearing as a stray fixed-position toast unrelated to the failing block's on-screen position. Cosmetic, not a data-loss or security issue; low priority. Would need to intercept/suppress mermaid's own DOM-injecting error path (e.g. via its internal error renderer config) or remove the stray node after each render attempt.
set.title: Mermaid's internal parse-error UI ('bomb' error graphic) injects into document.body instead of staying inside the failing block's container

set.body: Decision (user-confirmed): use the locally-installed `imagen` CLI (wraps Google's Gemini Imagen API, already configured with a working API key on this machine). Implemented full pipeline mirroring the diagram-gen pattern from story 1: src/lib/imageGen.ts (Bun-only, spawns imagen CLI to a temp file, reads+base64-encodes, cleans up temp file), src/lib/imageClient.ts (browser-safe entry routing through Tauri run_image_cli or dev-server POST /api/image), new Tauri run_image_cli command (base64 crate added), ImageGenExtension.tsx wired to the real call, removed the CSP-violating placehold.co fallback. Images are stored as base64 data URIs directly on the node's src attribute (ponytail: mirrors how DiagramGenExtension stores rendered content inline; avoids needing workspace-relative file paths / Tauri asset-protocol plumbing for v1 -- upgrade path is real file storage if doc-size bloat becomes a problem). Verified end-to-end live in-browser with a real (non-mocked) imagen call producing a real 1408px PNG.

Motion has real features and no way to know whether they work. The web mode designed as the browser-automation test surface never became real: WebStorage fakes writes and fakes openFolder, so testing saves against it proves nothing. set.body: Found by the first console baseline measurement in Phase 0. The welcome document serializes an unset diagram as 'content: null'. Three extensions each carried their own copy of the key:value parser, and all three turned that into the 4-character string "null" -- truthy, so DiagramGenExtension's render guard let it through and mermaid threw UnknownDiagramError on every page load. Fixed by extracting one shared parser (blockAttrs.ts) treating serialized null/undefined as unset, and pointing Dataset/ImageGen/DiagramGen at it. ImageGen had the same latent defect via 'src: null'.
set.title: Welcome doc's diagram-gen block sent the string "null" to mermaid.render on every cold load

set.body: Found while proving the E2E network gate actually bites. server.ts fell through to the SPA shell for ANY unmatched path, so fetch() for a missing note returned HTTP 200 carrying a page of HTML. WebStorage.readFile checks res.ok, so it treated that as a successful read and handed the editor HTML source as the note's markdown -- worse than the 'error loading file' behaviour B2 was thought to have. It also made missing files structurally invisible to the network gate. Fixed: unknown /api/* returns 404 JSON, a missing path whose last segment has a file extension returns 404, and only extensionless routes fall through to the SPA shell. /favicon.ico now answers 204 so the browser's unprompted request is not gate noise.
set.title: Dev server answered every missing file with 200 + index.html instead of 404

set.body: list_markdown_files used to overwrite WorkspaceState with any directory passed to it -- a second write path into the jail that bypassed the folder dialog, so any caller could silently re-root the sandbox. Phase 1 made the commands thin wrappers over fs_core; the listing command now only reads the stored root and validates the requested path is inside it.
set.title: B14 fixed: list_markdown_files no longer re-roots the workspace jail

set.body: Bun.serve defaults to hostname 0.0.0.0 when none is given, so the dev server listened on every interface. It already exposed /api/llm and /api/image, which spawn local subprocesses, and Phase 1 added /api/fs/write on top -- so anything on the same network could write files inside the workspace and run CLI tools, with no authentication. The workspace jail constrains where a write lands; it says nothing about who may ask. Now binds 127.0.0.1, overridable via MOTION_HOST. Also removed the Google Fonts entries still sitting in the Tauri CSP after the font links were dropped -- permissions granted for something the app no longer does. Surfaced by the design-doc generation pass reading the code end to end.
set.title: Dev server bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing filesystem writes and subprocess spawning to the local network
